Storage Comparison
• 	S3: Object Storage
• 	S3 Glacier: Object Archival
• 	EBS volumes: Network storage for one EC2 instance at a time
• 	Instance Storage: Physical storage for your EC2 instance (high IOPS)
• 	EFS: Network File System for Linux instances, POSIX filesystem
• 	FSx for Windows: Network File System for Windows servers
• 	FSx for Lustre: High Performance Computing Linux file system
• 	FSx for NetApp ONTAP: High OS Compatibility
• 	FSx for OpenZFS: Managed ZFS file system
• 	Storage Gateway: S3 & FSx File Gateway, Volume Gateway (cache & stored), Tape Gateway
• 	Transfer Family: FTP, FTPS, SFTP interface on top of Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS
• 	DataSync: Schedule data sync from on-premises to AWS, or AWS to AWS
• 	Snowcone / Snowball / Snowmobile: to move large amount of data to the cloud, physically
• 	Database: for specific workloads, usually with indexing and querying

content.summary:
## Hybrid access and bulk transfer

Evaluate dataset size, available bandwidth, time window and operational constraints. For a large one-off transfer over constrained connectivity, an available AWS offline transfer offering can reduce the transfer bottleneck.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

The limiting resource is the site connection. Offline transfer can bypass that constraint, subject to current service availability and operational lead time. Acceleration cannot create more last-mile bandwidth than the site has.

### Avoid this trap

Do not assume a named appliance is available to every new customer or Region. Check current ordering eligibility; shipping, copy and import time also count toward the deadline.

### Apply it

A site must move a very large archive to AWS, but its WAN would take months. Network upgrades are not feasible. What is the best architectural next step?

**Recommended design:** Evaluate an available offline AWS transfer offering and include local copy, shipping and import time in the migration plan.

The limiting resource is the site connection. Offline transfer can bypass that constraint, subject to current service availability and operational lead time. Acceleration cannot create more last-mile bandwidth than the site has.

cards.question: What physical limit can acceleration not eliminate?
When should offline bulk transfer be evaluated?
cards.answer: When network transfer cannot meet the migration window.

quiz.question: A site must move a very large archive to AWS, but its WAN would take months. Network upgrades are not feasible. What is the best architectural next step?
options: Evaluate an available offline AWS transfer offering and include local copy, shipping and import time in the migration plan.
Use Transfer Acceleration and assume it removes the physical limit of the local WAN.
Open more TCP sessions and assume a fixed-bandwidth link gains unlimited capacity.
Use Multi-AZ RDS to import arbitrary archive files from the site.
quiz.explanation: The limiting resource is the site connection. Offline transfer can bypass that constraint, subject to current service availability and operational lead time. Acceleration cannot create more last-mile bandwidth than the site has.

Storage Comparison
• 	S3: Object Storage
• 	S3 Glacier: Object Archival
• 	EBS volumes: Network storage for one EC2 instance at a time
• 	Instance Storage: Physical storage for your EC2 instance (high IOPS)
• 	EFS: Network File System for Linux instances, POSIX filesystem
• 	FSx for Windows: Network File System for Windows servers
• 	FSx for Lustre: High Performance Computing Linux file system
• 	FSx for NetApp ONTAP: High OS Compatibility
• 	FSx for OpenZFS: Managed ZFS file system
• 	Storage Gateway: S3 & FSx File Gateway, Volume Gateway (cache & stored), Tape Gateway
• 	Transfer Family: FTP, FTPS, SFTP interface on top of Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS
• 	DataSync: Schedule data sync from on-premises to AWS, or AWS to AWS
• 	Snowcone / Snowball / Snowmobile: to move large amount of data to the cloud, physically
• 	Database: for specific workloads, usually with indexing and querying

## Windows and Linux file workloads

Use FSx for Windows File Server for Windows-oriented SMB and Active Directory integration. EFS targets managed NFS access. S3 targets object API access rather than native SMB shares.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

The required protocol and directory integration point to FSx for Windows File Server. EFS provides NFS, while S3 is object storage. Network reachability, availability mode, backup and permissions remain design tasks.

### Avoid this trap

Choose by protocol and application compatibility before price. Mounting an object abstraction does not guarantee the file semantics, permissions or locking the application expects.

### Apply it

A Windows application requires shared SMB storage integrated with the organization Active Directory. Which managed service is the direct fit?

**Recommended design:** Use FSx for Windows File Server with the appropriate directory and network configuration.
